item.title: A quicker climb up the literacy mountain: Why rigor and efficiency matter in early reading
item.description: In early literacy, the goal is simple but urgent: Help students become independent readers and writers. Every instructional decision we make either moves them closer to that goal or keeps them circling the mountain instead of climbing it.

item.title: A new PLC model that builds collective efficacy and fights teacher burnout
item.description: In schools across the country, teacher turnover and burnout have reached crisis levels. Educators are stretched thin, often working in isolation, and many professional learning communities (PLCs) fail to deliver meaningful results.

item.title: New CoSN report underscores importance of intentional, reliable edtech use
item.description: A purposeful commitment to responsible edtech use--and to professional development for teachers--is necessary to ensure edtech is innovative and transformational, according to CoSN's annual 2026 Driving K-12 Innovation Report.

item.title: Tips and tools to effectively differentiate learning for student engagement
item.description: As a paraprofessional for over 3 years and going on my 5th year as a certified special education resource teacher, I’ve learned that no two learners are ever quite the same.

item.title: Celebrating Teachers: Nominate Outstanding Educators for Crystal Apple Awards
item.description: School Specialty, a leading provider of learning environments, instructional solutions, and supplies for preK-12 education, is proud to celebrate outstanding educators with its 12th annual Crystal Apple Awards.

item.title: Fueling student passion for STEM with project-based learning
item.description: We live in an ever-evolving world, powered by advancements across STEM fields. Today, STEM has become increasingly intertwined with how we live our daily lives--from how we learn, to how we work, to entertainment and more.

item.title: Why schools and public libraries must unite–in summer and all year long
item.description: Some of the most effective literacy ecosystems today are those where schools and public libraries work not in parallel, but in partnership with parents and students.

item.title: A smarter way to modernize aging school facilities
item.description: School buildings quietly shape everything that happens inside them. When systems work as intended, learning moves forward uninterrupted. When they fail, instruction, safety, and trust can unravel quickly.

item.title: AI didn’t break homework: It exposed what was already broken
item.description: Who among us has never copied a homework answer in a hurry? Borrowed a friend’s paragraph? Accepted a parent’s “small correction” that eventually became a full rewrite?
